response:
READING

**1. What the two courses actually cost**

The relevant comparison is not £214,000 against £118,000 but £214,000 against £118,000 plus the permanent dead-mileage penalty that comes with Culverstone.

*Dead mileage:*
Culverstone is 3 miles further from the 44 stand. Each vehicle travels that extra 3 miles out and 3 miles back: 6 extra miles per vehicle per day.

22 vehicles × 313 days × 6 miles × £0.63 = **£26,029 per year**

*Net annual saving under KESTERWICK vs ARDENSHAW:*
£214,000 − £118,000 − £26,029 = **£69,971 per year**

*Capital committed under KESTERWICK:*
£40,000 deposit + £480,000 works = **£520,000**

*Simple payback:* £520,000 ÷ £69,971 = **7.4 years** against a 10-year lease.

*Net gain over the full ten-year term (before any Nethercote bridging):*
(10 × £69,971) − £520,000 = **£179,710** in KESTERWICK's favour.

KESTERWICK is therefore financially superior over the full term even before we consider bridging costs, planning slippage, or the bid advantage.

---

**2. Planning timeline against the critical dates**

Application validated: 2026-08-14. Three scenarios, working forward:

| Scenario | Consent | + 22 weeks occupation | Hallowbrand ends | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Target (13 wks) | ~2026-11-13 | **~2027-04-16** | 2027-11-30 | 7½ months in hand |
| Median (34 wks) | ~2027-04-09 | **~2027-09-11** | 2027-11-30 | 11 weeks in hand |
| Slowest (61 wks) | ~2027-10-15 | **~2028-03-17** | 2027-11-30 | 3½ months over |

In the target and median cases — which together represent the normal range — Culverstone is ready before the Hallowbrand lease expires. No Nethercote is needed.

Only the 61-week figure (the single worst outcome in three years of records) forces a bridging period. That gap runs from roughly 2027-12-01 to 2028-03-17, call it four months.

*Nethercote cost in the worst case:* 4 × £18,500 = **£74,000**

*KESTERWICK net gain after worst-case bridging:* £179,710 − £74,000 = **£105,710**

So even assuming the worst planning outcome ever recorded, KESTERWICK ends the decade over £100,000 ahead.

The Faskally deposit holds the site to 2028-06-30. Even in the worst case Culverstone is ready (~2028-03-17) inside that window.

---

**3. The bid: a compounding advantage**

Bids for the next 44/44A term are due 2027-09-14. In the median planning scenario Culverstone is ready roughly 2027-09-11 — essentially confirmed at bid time. In the target scenario it has been open for five months by then.

Depot cost goes in as a fixed line. A confirmed Culverstone depot costs the bid £96,000 a year less than a Hallowbrand depot. That is not just internal saving; it is a real competitive margin against any operator who must price a higher property cost. Winning or retaining a contract worth three more years of revenue on that network is worth far more than the margin between the two property costs.

Under ARDENSHAW the bid is priced to the penny — but at a higher penny. That certainty comes at a price.

---

**4. The workshop absence under the worst case**

If Nethercote is needed (worst-case planning), there is no workshop for up to four months. Maintenance and scheduled inspection work must be contracted out. That is an additional cost not captured above, and it is a genuine operational nuisance for 31 vehicles. It does not, however, change the conclusion: Nethercote is month-to-month and ends the day Culverstone opens.

---

**5. Cash**

Available: £640,000 + £200,000 facility = £840,000.
KESTERWICK draws £520,000 (deposit December 2026, works following consent), leaving ~£320,000 headroom plus the facility. Tight, but the drawdown is phased and the business is generating cash from operations throughout. ARDENSHAW requires no capital but commits £214,000 per year for ten years.

---

**6. Summary of the decision**

| Factor | ARDENSHAW | KESTERWICK |
|---|---|---|
| 10-year rent + dead mileage | £2,140,000 | £1,440,290 |
| Capital | nil | £520,000 |
| Worst-case bridging (Nethercote) | nil | £74,000 |
| **10-year total (worst case)** | **£2,140,000** | **£2,034,290** |
| Bid competitiveness | Higher fixed cost | £96k/yr lower fixed cost |
| Operational continuity | Certain | Certain in expected case; 4-month disruption in worst case |
| Commitment at end of term | Hallowbrand tenant | Culverstone owner of improvements |

The financial case for KESTERWICK holds in every planning scenario. The operational risk under the worst-case planning outcome is real but bounded and survivable. The bid advantage is a bonus that ARDENSHAW cannot match.

**I recommend KESTERWICK.** Pay Faskally by 5 December, let the Hallowbrand offer go, and build out Culverstone. Monitor the planning programme monthly; if the determination is running past 34 weeks, open dialogue with the county and move Nethercote vehicles in orderly fashion rather than in a scramble at lease-end.

---

READING
  Across all planning scenarios — target, median, and the single worst outcome on record — KESTERWICK costs less over the decade than ARDENSHAW: the rent gap (£96,000 a year) outpaces the dead-mileage penalty (£26,029 a year) and recoups the £520,000 capital outlay within 7.4 years, leaving a net gain of roughly £106,000 to £180,000 depending on planning duration, while also supplying a materially lower fixed-cost line for the 2027-09-14 bid. The worst-case operational exposure — four months at Nethercote without a workshop — is survivable given available cash and the month-to-month nature of that arrangement.

CALL
  KESTERWICK

GROUNDS
  In every planning scenario, including the single worst determination on record, KESTERWICK recovers its capital and ends the decade over £100,000 ahead of ARDENSHAW on a like-for-like basis, while simultaneously reducing the fixed cost line in the 2027 bid by £96,000 a year.
